description.narrative: The Project Development Objective is to contribute to improvement in the quality of care and in the financial sustainability of the health care systems in Republika Srpska and the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

The development objective of Health Systems Improvement Project is to contribute to improvement in the quality of care and in the financial sustainability of the health care systems in Republika Srpska and the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina. This project has two components. The first component, Increasing health system performance in Republika Srpska, has the following sub-components: Improving the efficiency and quality of health care; Improving the efficiency and quality of health car; Improving the efficiency and quality of health car; and Project management and monitoring. The second component, Increasing health systems performance in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, has the following sub-components: Improving the efficiency and quality of health care; Strengthening management and financial sustainability of health care institutions; and Project management and monitoring.

title.narrative: Transfers from the general government budget to the health insurance fund for the purposes of paying health care insurance for special categories of the population, '000 000 BAM

comment.narrative:
Data for this indicator are requested and will be provided as part of the next ISR.
This indicator measures transfers made from the government's regular budget to the health insurance fund, and from the health insurance fund and to health care providers, to maintain health insurance, and coverage of the health care needs, of war veterans, refugees, the unemployed, social welfare recipients, and other categories, as defined in Article 10(a) of the Law on Health Insurance published in Official Gazette No.18/99. It is a means to monitor the continuity and equity of access to healthcare systems as efficiency reforms are undertaken. The baseline value is maintained as the target value throughout the project cycle, and actual (current) values are measured annually and not cumulative.

title.narrative: The gap between the percentage of hypertensive men and the percentage of hypertensive women whose hypertension is adequately controlled, as defined by current clinical guidelines

comment.narrative:
The definition of the indicator, along with its baseline and target values, will be updated as part of the restructuring.
This indicator reflects the effectiveness of detecting and treating hypertension in primary care, directly supporting the achievement of PDO Indicator 2. Hypertensive men are less likely than women to be aware, treated, and controlled. Risk factors driving high blood pressure—smoking, poor diet, and heavy alcohol use—stem from social norms rather than biology, making them gender issues. The baseline value, 13%, represents the difference between 22.2% of hypertensive women who have safe blood pressure and 9% of hypertensive men who have safe blood pressure. Self-evidently, a decrease in the rate of control of hypertension in women to meet that of men will not count as success for this indicator. Rather, a levelling-up in the rate of control across both genders is expected.

title.narrative: The percentage of health care providers achieving a debt ratio of 0.5 or less at the end of the financial year

comment.narrative:
Data is requested in both RS and FBIH and will be available in the next reporting period.
Debt ratio = total debt / total assets. This indicator measures the effectiveness of financial management within health care facilities in both RS and FBiH. It captures longer term financial stability (by including assets) and can also reflect progress in reducing arrears (a subset of liabilities). It is well-established internationally as a measure of financial health. Baseline value will be confirmed during the first months of project implementation.

title.narrative: The percentage reduction in the rate of hospital admissions where the only recorded diagnosis is arterial hypertension, or where the principal diagnosis is uncomplicated arterial hypertension

baseline.value: To be defined within the first year of the project

comment.narrative:
The baseline is confirmed in RS for 2024. The data in FBIH is available for a limited number of hospitals. The data request and instruction for FBIH cantons is being prepared.
Uncomplicated arterial hypertension is chosen because, in a high-performing health system, it is almost always treatable in primary care and almost never a valid reason for hospital admission. This indicator, therefore, measures the quality and efficiency of the health care network, ensuring more management by primary care and avoiding unnecessary hospitalization, in both RS and the FBiH. Attention to this indicator should also improve the accuracy of clinical coding upon a patient's admission or discharge (and thereby improve understanding of hospital activity and ensure correct reimbursement). The value is the number of admissions per 100,000 population.
